imageStorage.descCreate: Set up a new image hosting provider for your resort.
imageStorage.descView: View your image hosting config details.
imageStorage.descEdit: Update your image hosting config name.
imageStorage.name: Config name
imageStorage.helpS3Body:
1. Sign in to the AWS Console and open the S3 service.
2. Create a bucket (or use an existing one) and note the Bucket Name and Region.
3. Open IAM → Users → Create a user with programmatic access.
4. Attach the AmazonS3FullAccess policy (or a scoped bucket policy).
5. Download or copy the Access Key ID and Secret Access Key — the secret is only shown once.
imageStorage.helpCloudinaryBody:
1. Sign in to your Cloudinary account at cloudinary.com.
2. From the Dashboard, find your Cloud Name at the top of the page.
3. Scroll down to the API Keys section to find your API Key and API Secret.
4. The API Secret is masked by default — click the eye icon to reveal it.
imageStorage.helpTitle: What is an image hosting config?
imageStorage.helpBody:
An image hosting config stores the credentials for a cloud provider (Cloudinary or Amazon S3) used to upload and serve your resort's images.

To configure Cloudinary, you need your Cloud Name, API Key, and API Secret from the Cloudinary dashboard.

To configure Amazon S3, you need your Bucket Name, AWS Region, Access Key ID, and Secret Access Key from the AWS IAM console.

Once added, you can select a config when uploading images such as your resort logo.
